title: Okapi: Decoupling Data Striping and Redundancy Grouping in Cluster File Systems
problem: Traditional cluster file systems couple data striping (for parallelism) with redundancy grouping (for fault tolerance), limiting flexibility and efficiency in data placement and recovery strategies.
motivation: Decoupling striping and redundancy enables independent optimization of performance and fault tolerance characteristics, improving overall system efficiency.
method: Okapi decouples data striping and redundancy grouping mechanisms, allowing separate optimization of performance-oriented data distribution and reliability-oriented redundancy strategies.
key_novelty: Decoupled architecture for data striping and redundancy in cluster file systems enabling independent optimization.
contributions: Decoupled striping and redundancy grouping model
Improved fault tolerance and performance characteristics

metrics.other: Storage efficiency and fault recovery performance

limitations: Complexity of managing decoupled strategies; applicability to diverse failure scenarios requires validation.
